nodes.label: Statistical Learning of Attentional Priority
nodes.definition: Learning of regularities in the environment that biases later attentional priority even without explicit current instruction.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Learned environmental regularities can alter selection history, but effects must be separated from current goals and simple repetition.
failure_modes: Do not infer Statistical Learning of Attentional Priority from a single output metric.
Do not treat Statistical Learning of Attentional Priority as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Repetition Priming of Selection
nodes.definition: Facilitation or bias in selection caused by recent repetition of target, feature, or selection episodes.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Repetition can shape later selection but should not be equated with reward-driven attention or long-term habit.
failure_modes: Do not infer Repetition Priming of Selection from a single output metric.
Do not treat Repetition Priming of Selection as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Temporal Stability of Attention
nodes.definition: Degree to which attentional engagement remains stable rather than fluctuating across time within a task or exposure.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Attentional stability reflects multiple processes including alertness, lapses and mind wandering and needs task-specific measurement.
failure_modes: Do not infer Temporal Stability of Attention from a single output metric.
Do not treat Temporal Stability of Attention as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Interference Control
nodes.definition: Ability/process of limiting disruption from competing representations, responses, or task-irrelevant information.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Interference control overlaps executive attention and working-memory control but is distinguishable from simple distractor suppression.
failure_modes: Do not infer Interference Control from a single output metric.
Do not treat Interference Control as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Inhibitory Attentional Control
nodes.definition: Control processes that reduce or prevent attentional allocation to information that conflicts with current goals.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Inhibitory-control terminology spans several mechanisms; this node remains provisional until proactive/reactive and attention/response inhibition are separated.
failure_modes: Do not infer Inhibitory Attentional Control from a single output metric.
Do not treat Inhibitory Attentional Control as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Incentive Salience
nodes.definition: Motivational prominence or 'wanting' assigned to reward-associated cues, potentially dissociable from expected utility or experienced liking.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Incentive salience is not identical to reward value, pleasure, or attention; transport from reward-neuroscience paradigms requires caution.
failure_modes: Do not infer Incentive Salience from a single output metric.
Do not treat Incentive Salience as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Physiological Activation
nodes.definition: Autonomic or bodily activation associated with emotional/motivational states.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Physiological activation is multiply determined and cannot identify a specific emotion, appraisal, or motivational direction on its own.
failure_modes: Do not infer Physiological Activation from a single output metric.
Do not treat Physiological Activation as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Anticipated Relief
nodes.definition: Expected future relief from removal, reduction, or avoidance of an aversive state or problem.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Anticipated relief can motivate action but is distinct from actual experienced relief and from generic reward anticipation.
failure_modes: Do not infer Anticipated Relief from a single output metric.
Do not treat Anticipated Relief as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Goal Shielding
nodes.definition: Protection of an active focal goal from interference by competing goals, temptations, or distractions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Goal shielding supports persistence but can also narrow attention and create opportunity costs.
failure_modes: Do not infer Goal Shielding from a single output metric.
Do not treat Goal Shielding as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Extrinsic Motivation
nodes.definition: Motivation to act for outcomes separable from the inherent enjoyment of the activity, ranging from externally controlled to highly internalized forms.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Extrinsic motivation is heterogeneous; it must not be equated with controlled motivation or monetary reward alone.
failure_modes: Do not infer Extrinsic Motivation from a single output metric.
Do not treat Extrinsic Motivation as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Group-Based Depersonalization
nodes.definition: Shift in self-perception from unique personal identity toward seeing the self as an interchangeable exemplar of a salient group category.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Depersonalization in self-categorization theory is not loss of personhood; it is category-based self-definition.
failure_modes: Do not infer Group-Based Depersonalization from a single output metric.
Do not treat Group-Based Depersonalization as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Perceived Norm Discrepancy
nodes.definition: Perceived gap between one's own behavior/belief and the descriptive or injunctive norm attributed to a relevant group.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Norm discrepancy can motivate alignment, resistance, concealment, or identity defense depending on identification and autonomy.
failure_modes: Do not infer Perceived Norm Discrepancy from a single output metric.
Do not treat Perceived Norm Discrepancy as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Request Susceptibility
nodes.definition: Context-specific likelihood of complying with a request as a function of requester, relationship, authority, norms, framing and recipient state.
nodes.mechanism_summary: There is no single stable global susceptibility to requests; this node is a runtime/context abstraction rather than a trait claim.
failure_modes: Do not infer Request Susceptibility from a single output metric.
Do not treat Request Susceptibility as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Interpersonal Attraction
nodes.definition: Positive social attraction toward another person that can support liking, affiliation and receptivity.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Attraction is distinct from trustworthiness, expertise, similarity and group identification even though they can interact.
failure_modes: Do not infer Interpersonal Attraction from a single output metric.
Do not treat Interpersonal Attraction as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Communal Orientation
nodes.definition: Orientation toward relationships in which parties attend to each other's needs without strict immediate exchange accounting.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Communal orientation is relationship-specific and should not be inferred from warmth, reciprocity, or belonging cues alone.
failure_modes: Do not infer Communal Orientation from a single output metric.
Do not treat Communal Orientation as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Satisficing
nodes.definition: Decision strategy of selecting an option that meets an acceptability threshold rather than exhaustively optimizing across all alternatives.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Satisficing can be adaptive under constraints and should not be treated as low-quality decision making by definition.
failure_modes: Do not infer Satisficing from a single output metric.
Do not treat Satisficing as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Endowment Valuation / Endowment Effect
nodes.definition: Higher valuation sometimes observed for an object or option when it is owned or treated as endowed relative to otherwise comparable nonownership conditions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Endowment effects are heterogeneous and should not automatically be attributed to loss aversion.
failure_modes: Do not infer Endowment Valuation / Endowment Effect from a single output metric.
Do not treat Endowment Valuation / Endowment Effect as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Uncertainty Tolerance
nodes.definition: Degree to which a person is willing to accept unresolved, probabilistic, ambiguous, or incomplete information in a decision context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Tolerance is domain- and context-sensitive and overlaps but is not identical to ambiguity aversion or risk preference.
failure_modes: Do not infer Uncertainty Tolerance from a single output metric.
Do not treat Uncertainty Tolerance as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Compromise Resolution
nodes.definition: Resolution of attribute conflict by selecting an intermediate option that avoids extremes on competing dimensions.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Compromise choice depends on set structure and conflict; it is not a universal preference for middle options.
failure_modes: Do not infer Compromise Resolution from a single output metric.
Do not treat Compromise Resolution as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Relative Evaluation
nodes.definition: Evaluation of a target partly in relation to other available or salient alternatives rather than only on absolute properties.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Relative evaluation creates context sensitivity and can interact with anchors, contrast and attribute ranges.
failure_modes: Do not infer Relative Evaluation from a single output metric.
Do not treat Relative Evaluation as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Claim Plausibility
nodes.definition: Perceived compatibility of a claim with prior knowledge, causal expectations, base beliefs, and contextual evidence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Plausibility can affect claim acceptance but is not equivalent to factual truth; false claims can appear plausible and true claims implausible.
failure_modes: Do not infer Claim Plausibility from a single output metric.
Do not treat Claim Plausibility as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Mechanism / Causal-Explanation Credibility
nodes.definition: Perceived credibility of an explanation for how or why a claimed effect would occur.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Mechanistic explanation can support understanding or credibility, but an intuitively satisfying mechanism is not causal proof.
failure_modes: Do not infer Mechanism / Causal-Explanation Credibility from a single output metric.
Do not treat Mechanism / Causal-Explanation Credibility as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Epistemic Confidence
nodes.definition: Confidence in the correctness or truth status of knowledge, beliefs, or informational judgments.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Epistemic confidence overlaps belief strength and judgment confidence; exact boundaries depend on the target of confidence.
failure_modes: Do not infer Epistemic Confidence from a single output metric.
Do not treat Epistemic Confidence as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Judgment Confidence
nodes.definition: Subjective confidence in a specific evaluative or decision judgment.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Confidence affects reliance on judgments but can be miscalibrated and should be distinguished from objective accuracy.
failure_modes: Do not infer Judgment Confidence from a single output metric.
Do not treat Judgment Confidence as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Word-Order Processing
nodes.definition: Processing consequences of the order in which sentence constituents and dependent elements are arranged.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Word order interacts with syntactic expectations, dependency length, information structure and language-specific grammar.
failure_modes: Do not infer Word-Order Processing from a single output metric.
Do not treat Word-Order Processing as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Pragmatic Inference
nodes.definition: Context-sensitive inference used to derive intended communicative meaning beyond literal encoded content.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Pragmatic inference integrates utterance, common ground, alternatives, goals and social reasoning.
failure_modes: Do not infer Pragmatic Inference from a single output metric.
Do not treat Pragmatic Inference as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Anaphora / Reference Resolution
nodes.definition: Process of identifying which prior or contextual entity a referring expression denotes.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Reference resolution depends on discourse representation, salience, syntax, semantics and common ground.
failure_modes: Do not infer Anaphora / Reference Resolution from a single output metric.
Do not treat Anaphora / Reference Resolution as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Discourse Inference
nodes.definition: Inference used to connect explicit discourse content, fill causal or referential gaps, and build coherent situation models.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Inferences support coherence but vary in necessity, cost and dependence on world knowledge.
failure_modes: Do not infer Discourse Inference from a single output metric.
Do not treat Discourse Inference as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Given–New Ordering
nodes.definition: Organization of linguistic information according to what is treated as already established versus newly introduced in discourse.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Given–new organization interacts with focus, coherence and audience knowledge and is not a rigid word-order rule across languages.
failure_modes: Do not infer Given–New Ordering from a single output metric.
Do not treat Given–New Ordering as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Speaker / Message Stance
nodes.definition: Linguistic and rhetorical positioning of the speaker toward claims, certainty, values, evidence, audience and alternatives.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Stance is a design property whose effects depend on credibility, pragmatics, identity and audience expectations.
failure_modes: Do not infer Speaker / Message Stance from a single output metric.
Do not treat Speaker / Message Stance as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Rhetorical Credibility Positioning
nodes.definition: Deliberate presentation choices intended to position a source as credible, trustworthy, expert, transparent or aligned with audience values.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Credibility positioning must remain separate from actual receiver-side credibility judgments and factual source quality.
failure_modes: Do not infer Rhetorical Credibility Positioning from a single output metric.
Do not treat Rhetorical Credibility Positioning as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Transformation Arc
nodes.definition: Narrative organization around a meaningful transition from an initial state through events or conflict to a changed later state.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Transformation can organize stories and before–after claims, but persuasive effects depend on coherence, evidence, identification and relevance.
failure_modes: Do not infer Transformation Arc from a single output metric.
Do not treat Transformation Arc as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.

nodes.label: Concession
nodes.definition: Deliberate acknowledgment of a limitation, opposing point, uncertainty, or disadvantage within an advocated message.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Concession can support two-sidedness or credibility but effects depend on what is conceded, placement, refutation and audience prior beliefs.
failure_modes: Do not infer Concession from a single output metric.
Do not treat Concession as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Request Framing
nodes.definition: Way a requested action is linguistically and contextually presented, including politeness, norm cues, autonomy support, benefit/cost framing and social context.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Request framing can alter compliance, but no single framing pattern is universally superior and effects interact with reactance, authority, reciprocity and friction.
failure_modes: Do not infer Request Framing from a single output metric.
Do not treat Request Framing as a universal persuasion effect without boundary conditions.
open_questions: Requires further construct discrimination or direct evidence before strong runtime use.
